# Produce a merchant release from one Git commit

Use the maintained `build.mjs` in a current source checkout. It selects the
distribution specification, component files, native dependency versions and
relative ESM import closure from one resolved commit. The worktree can contain
other work; the selected Git snapshot determines the complete package.

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --repo /absolute/public-commons-sprint-2026 \
  --ref FULL_COMMIT_SHA \
  --out /absolute/new-merchant-release
```

Node, npm and Git with `--no-lazy-fetch` support are required. The builder emits
phase progress on stderr and the final JSON receipt on stdout. The original
native command worker can retain those streams together with
`new-merchant-release/distribution.json`. This works with an ordinary checkout
or a bare repository whose chosen commit and trees are already available.

## Source acquisition and reuse

The source reader resolves the ref once, reads that commit's tree, and inspects
the selected blobs in batches. It disables replacement objects and implicit
lazy fetching so each source read has a known identity and acquisition step.
Existing Git object storage and configured alternates supply cached bytes.

For a partial clone, missing selected blobs are requested together from its
existing promisor remotes. The first batch obtains the specification and
license; subsequent batches obtain selected components and any newly discovered
static imports. Each request contains exact blob IDs from the chosen tree.
Acquisition leaves branch refs, the checkout and `FETCH_HEAD` in place, and
does not start automatic Git maintenance. The repository keeps the objects for
the next operation. Use an existing clone and its ordinary authenticated Git
configuration when access is required.

After acquisition, the reader checks each blob's type, declared size, complete
batch framing and Git object hash before passing its original bytes to the
builder. The reader and builder share a 128 MiB aggregate source limit, while
original source files retain their 2 MiB limit. Before materialization, the whole
package—including its generated manifest, metadata, README and license—must fit
the original installer's 128 MiB unpacked limit and 4 MiB member limit. The final
compressed archive remains limited to 64 MiB. Use the maintained object receiver,
builder and runtime installer from this source edition together when producing a
cumulative package above the earlier 64 MiB unpacked limit. Earlier original
archives remain supported. The regular-file restrictions, complete component
inventory, static-import parsing and pinned runtime dependency rules remain part
of packaging.

Source-owned `supportFiles` may retain explicitly named CSV, JSON, TXT and
Parquet data inside an original `fixtures` directory. This keeps a receiver's
published input paths, manifests and hashes intact. Parquet and ZIP files require
an explicit declaration; they are not selected automatically from a component.
Executable fixtures, test directories and hidden paths remain excluded. Declared
data still passes the original regular-file, explicit-exclusion, Git identity,
individual-file and complete-package checks.

The progress stream reports the resolved commit, selected file count, source
inspection, each fetch, bytes loaded, materialization, npm packaging and final
archive hash. It carries configured remote names instead of credential-bearing
remote URLs. The final `sourceAcquisition` receipt records Git command count,
metadata/content batches, fetched and cached object counts, unique bytes and
timing. These measurements are outside the archive so the same selected source
retains the same package bytes.

## Repeat the build offline

After the source objects are present, use a new output directory:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --repo /absolute/public-commons-sprint-2026 \
  --ref FULL_COMMIT_SHA \
  --out /absolute/merchant-release-offline \
  --offline
```

This option prevents source acquisition. Missing objects produce
`MISSING_SOURCE_OBJECTS` with the selected commit and object IDs in the
programmatic error. The CLI identifies the missing count and the recovery
action. Acquire those objects in the same repository, then repeat the selected
commit. If materialization or packaging has already created the output, continue
that original directory with `--resume` as described below.

The completed output contains the original npm archive, `distribution.json`,
and an inspectable `package/` directory. `package/manifest.json` maps every
included original path to its Git blob, SHA-256, byte count and mode. Install
the archive and use its maintained `starforge` command as described in the
[merchant guide](README.md). Component owners can consume that exact archive
and manifest while later source changes continue toward the following release.

## Continue an interrupted build

On Linux, resume in the original output directory after restoring available
disk space or ending the interrupted operation's original process:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --repo /absolute/public-commons-sprint-2026 \
  --out /absolute/new-merchant-release --resume --offline
```

The retained `build.json` binds the output to one source commit, package version
and exact manifest. With no `--ref`, resume selects that saved commit even when
the repository's current branch has advanced. An explicitly supplied ref must
resolve to the same commit. Existing Git object storage supplies the selected
source, and the original specification, browser mappings, import closure and
dependency selection still determine the package.

Completed source files retain their existing bytes and inode. A partially
written file continues only after its existing bytes match the exact original
prefix. Missing files are written into the same stage. Conflicting bytes, an
unexpected file or a linked directory stop that specific operation with the
affected path. The builder never substitutes the current branch's newer source.
Progress and the final receipt report copied, resumed and reused file counts
and the number of bytes actually written by the continuation.

The original `npm pack --ignore-scripts --json` runs inside the same output's
`pack-work/` directory. Its archive is linked into the final output without
copying it. Linux keeps the original open-description file lock with npm, so a
surviving pack process remains the sole writer when its parent exits. A second
invocation reports `DISTRIBUTION_BUILD_ALREADY_RUNNING`; it does not infer that
a process in another namespace is stale or start another pack against it.

If npm finished before its result was retained, the existing original release
reader verifies the archive against the retained manifest and complete source
stage. That completed archive is then reused. This particular recovery needs
Python 3.11+; select an installed interpreter with `--python EXECUTABLE`.
A truncated, unacknowledged archive in the builder's private pack work area can
be removed and packed again after its bytes and failed state are inspected.
An acknowledged archive or final delivery with conflicting bytes remains
available for diagnosis. Final archive and receipt publication use exclusive
links and durable records, so interruption cannot overwrite an existing result.

Repeating `--resume` after completion returns the original archive, integrity
and receipt with `reused: true`. With no ref, or the same full source commit,
that path does not read Git, parse source or invoke npm again. The original
archive is hashed as a stream when reopening its receipt.

Inspect retained progress without acquiring source or starting a build:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --out /absolute/new-merchant-release --status
```

Status reports retained materialization or completion, the pinned commit and
available result. It describes the saved files; it does not declare a process
alive or release its lock.

Older output directories can also continue. An existing original
`package/manifest.json` supplies their source commit. For a legacy partial stage
without that manifest, specify its original full commit with `--ref`. The same
complete inventory and prefix comparison adopt only the declared package
files. Fresh builds keep the existing new-directory behavior; `--resume` is an
explicit choice and incomplete recovery uses Linux's native `flock`.

## Programmatic build

```js
import { buildDistribution } from './build.mjs';

const receipt = await buildDistribution({
  repository: '/absolute/public-commons-sprint-2026',
  ref: 'FULL_COMMIT_SHA',
  output: '/absolute/new-merchant-release',
  offline: false,
  onProgress: event => process.stderr.write(JSON.stringify(event) + '\n'),
});
```

Existing callers can keep the original arguments. `offline` and `onProgress` add
offline source reads and structured progress; the existing receipt fields
retain their meaning. `npm pack --ignore-scripts` remains the packaging step.

Pass `resume: true` to `buildDistribution` to continue the same `output` and omit
`ref` to use its retained pin. `python` selects the interpreter for the original
archive verifier when recovering an unacknowledged completed pack. The exported
`inspectDistributionBuild({ output })` provides the same retained state as
`--status`.

Git references: [batch object reads](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-cat-file),
[partial clone acquisition](https://git-scm.com/docs/partial-clone),
[explicit fetch input](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-fetch), and
[`--no-lazy-fetch`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git).


## Package an audience-specific product

A standalone product repository can keep the original source layout, native commands and build lifecycle while selecting its own customer-facing package metadata. Declare the optional `product` object in its committed base `distribution.json`:

```json
{
  "product": {
    "schema": "stellar-forge.merchant-product-package.v1",
    "description": "TokenJunkieLabs Stellar merchant workspace and material catalog operations",
    "repository": {
      "url": "https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace",
      "directory": ""
    },
    "readme": "products/material-catalog/README.md",
    "bin": {
      "starforge": "products/material-catalog/cli.mjs"
    }
  }
}
```

All fields after `schema` are optional. An absent `product` keeps the existing package metadata exactly. The repository URL must identify one public GitHub repository; its optional directory and every README or executable target are normalized source-relative paths. The builder rejects unknown fields, parent traversal, URL query/fragment text and unsupported entrypoints. A product can declare one to eight named Node commands.

Select each declared executable and README in the ordinary `components` or `supportFiles` inventory. Missing or explicitly excluded product entries fail before a package is materialized. Keep only the product's required native components, source-owned contribution files, dynamic runtime inputs and browser assets in that repository. The existing static-import closure, dependency manifests, archive limits and publication lifecycle apply to the complete selected source.

The selected Git commit remains the build identity. The complete base declaration, including product metadata, remains in `distributionInputs` with its original Git blob and byte digest. `manifest.sourceRepository` and npm repository metadata identify the standalone product; retain upstream source pins and legitimate third-party licenses in that repository when copying maintained source. Resume uses the same pinned declaration and refuses a changed manifest. Use the ordinary `build.mjs --repo PRODUCT_CHECKOUT --ref COMMIT --out OUTPUT` invocation; the product introduces no second packaging engine.

# Receive an original Git source cache

The Git object receiver carries an exact published source snapshot to the
maintained distribution builder when a complete source archive or an existing
Git fetch is unavailable. It can reuse a completed source installation and
existing Git object databases. Those donors stay read only.

The receiving result is an ordinary private Git object cache. The current
`buildDistribution`, archive inspection, runtime profile review, installation,
managed adoption, and Applications lifecycle continue to own their original
steps.

## Inputs and original source identity

Capture these inputs from the selected repository revision:

- The immutable commit ID and original root tree ID.
- A complete recursive GitData tree response with `truncated: false`.
- The exact UTF-8 commit object body in `commitText`.
- The original regular file paths selected by the maintained builder.

The receiver checks the commit's Git object hash before writing anything. It
reconstructs every directory tree with Git's mode, byte ordering, names, and raw
object IDs and checks every resulting tree hash. The root must match the commit.

A GitData commit response expresses dates in UTC, while the original Git
commit also retains the author's and committer's timezone offsets. Preserve the
original raw object from an existing Git donor where possible. A reconstructed
candidate is usable only after its complete Git object ID matches the selected
commit. The original MPP operation at
`9ef475062876557d6baf14e0e5414d7afbf3bc7f` uses `-0400` for both offsets.

Metadata may be supplied as UTF-8 JSON or a single gzip-compressed JSON member. Both retain an 8 MiB decompressed limit; the immutable metadata digest is calculated from the same canonical JSON regardless of carrier compression.

The metadata file has this shape:

```json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.git-object-receiving.v1",
  "source": {
    "repository": "owner/repository",
    "commit": "40-character original commit ID",
    "tree": "40-character original root tree ID"
  },
  "commitText": "tree ...\nparent ...\nauthor ...\ncommitter ...\n\noriginal message",
  "tree": {
    "sha": "40-character original root tree ID",
    "truncated": false,
    "tree": [
      {
        "path": "path/to/file.mjs",
        "mode": "100644",
        "type": "blob",
        "sha": "40-character original blob ID",
        "size": 1234
      }
    ]
  },
  "requiredPaths": ["LICENSE", "path/to/file.mjs"]
}
```

The real tree contains every directory and file record. The receiver requires
all intermediate tree entries. The abbreviated record above illustrates the
field layout.

## Receive from existing source

Use the same Git executable required by the maintained builder, including
`--no-lazy-fetch` support, and an owned private cache directory.

```sh
python3 git-object-receiving.py \
  --metadata /private/captured-source.json \
  --commit ORIGINAL_COMMIT \
  --directory /private/source-receiving \
  --donor-repository /existing/complete-source.git \
  --donor-source /existing/runtime/package/source \
  --incoming /private/received-original-blobs
```

Each donor argument is repeatable. Existing Git donors are read with the
original Git batch metadata and content interfaces. The receiver suppresses
lazy fetching and never changes their refs, object databases, alternates, or
configuration. File donors are read only at original selected paths, and their
bytes are accepted by exact Git blob ID.

The receiver also accepts native provider captures placed in the incoming
directory as `OBJECT_ID.blob`, containing the complete raw original bytes, or `OBJECT_ID.blob.gz` with one gzip member. The gzip carrier has the same 2 MiB decompressed source-file limit and rejects concatenated members and trailing compressed content. Preserve binary content and final newlines exactly. Each file's decompressed byte length and Git blob hash must match its original tree entry before it enters the cache.

The JSON result identifies the original source, owned cache path, verified tree
count, requested source size, donor contributions, and remaining original
objects. Exit code 2 writes `missing-objects.json`, which supplies each missing
object ID, original byte length, and selected paths. Acquire that exact set
through the existing provider/source transfer and repeat the same command.

Exit code 0 reports `OBJECTS_AVAILABLE`. All requested object bytes and complete
original tree metadata are then available in `repository.git`.

## Receive directly from a retained release

A completed merchant release can supply original blobs without another package
extraction. Pass its retained SHA-256 and absolute file path as one repeatable
`--donor-archive` pair alongside the current Git or source donors:

```sh
python3 git-object-receiving.py \
  --metadata /private/captured-source.json \
  --commit ORIGINAL_COMMIT \
  --directory /private/source-receiving \
  --donor-repository /existing/complete-source.git \
  --donor-archive ARCHIVE_SHA256 /existing/merchant-release.tgz \
  --materialize /private/original-consumer/source
```

The receiver checks the entire original archive digest before receiving any
member. It opens one regular file, streams its gzip/tar contents and matches
member bytes to missing objects in the selected Git tree. The archive can come
from an earlier or later release: only exact matching Git blob IDs and original
byte lengths enter the current immutable cache. Package prefixes and member
names do not affect matching. Archive paths and link targets are never
extracted or executed.

Compressed archives retain a 64 MiB limit. The expanded stream, including tar
headers, padding and skipped members, has a 256 MiB limit. This framing allowance
is separate from the 128 MiB aggregate selected-source limit and the original
2 MiB limit for an individual accepted source file. Metadata remains bounded to
8 MiB. The receiver consumes gzip checksums and verifies that the opened archive
stayed unchanged during the read.

The existing `donors` result adds an `original-release-archive` entry with its
archive path, checked SHA-256, compressed and expanded sizes, regular member
count and contributed object count. All Git/source/flat-blob donors, missing
object requests, cache resumption and source materialization keep their
existing contracts. An interrupted read can leave only independently verified
source blobs; resume the same original cache and archive.

## Receive a complete source snapshot in ZIP parts

When the available file service cannot carry the whole original source archive,
the same receiver accepts a complete manifested transfer:

```sh
python3 /existing/toolkit/git-object-receiving.py \
  --source-transfer /private/huwise-source/Huwise_Source_d1868_TRANSFER.json \
  --commit d1868cba6fd5f3b57e0445a094da8a3d4002b00e \
  --directory /private/huwise-source-receiving
```

Keep the original index beside its downloaded ZIP files, using each exact
relative filename and byte length recorded in the index. The download stage
owns HTTP continuation and destination delivery. The receiver reads those local
files and puts their original source objects directly into its existing
`repository.git` cache. ZIP contents never become extraction paths.

The captured Huwise source transfer contains 18 ZIP parts carrying the original
4,940 files and 65,179,698 source bytes at commit
`d1868cba6fd5f3b57e0445a094da8a3d4002b00e`. Its original root tree is
`9e4112bc3da8a93aaa1eab045330ff96ae23c7d6`. The ZIPs total 22,369,451 bytes.
This mode receives all original regular source files, so the maintained builder
can resolve the selected product's dependency closure offline. A Huwise release
then uses the existing source selection:

```sh
node /existing/toolkit/build.mjs \
  --repo /private/huwise-source-receiving/repository.git \
  --ref d1868cba6fd5f3b57e0445a094da8a3d4002b00e \
  --selection huwise \
  --offline \
  --out /private/original-huwise-release
```

The builder retains its own original output directory and `--resume`
contract. The received cache retains the selected historical revision, including
that revision's own tools. A newer receiving tool runs from its existing toolkit
location; receiving source does not replace historical files with newer tool
bytes. Use `--materialize /private/original-source` only when the original
consumer needs a complete source directory as well as the object cache.

### Transfer index and per-part contract

The immutable UTF-8 JSON index uses schema
`stellar-forge.git-source-transfer.v1`. It contains:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `source.repository` | Original GitHub owner/repository. |
| `source.commit`, `source.tree` | Original commit and full recursive root tree. |
| `source.fileCount`, `source.sourceBytes` | Complete original regular-file count and byte total. |
| `parts` | Ordered, contiguous records numbered from 1. |
| `parts[].path`, `archiveBytes` | Exact local ZIP filename and compressed byte length. |
| `carrierCommit`, `carrierTree` | Git source-carrier identities, separate from the product commit. |
| `manifestGitBlob`, `manifestSha256`, `manifestBytes` | Exact manifest bytes under Git and SHA-256, with byte length. |
| `kind`, `sourceFiles`, `sourceBytes` | Authority or source-file part, and its original source totals. |
| `archiveSha256` | Optional previously captured ZIP digest; checked when present. |
| `sourceUrl`, `notionReference` | Optional original delivery references used by the download stage. |

Every ZIP has GitHub's one enclosing directory. At its root,
`SOURCE-PART.json` uses schema `stellar-forge.git-source-part.v1` and
repeats the original `source`, part number, total part count and kind.
Each original source member declares `path`, `mode`, `gitBlob`
and `bytes`. Paths and executable modes are the original Git values.

Part 1 is the sole `git-authority` part. It carries the exact
`SOURCE-COMMIT.json` GitData commit response and
`SOURCE-TREE.json` complete recursive tree response. Its
`authorities` array declares each filename, kind, byte length and SHA-256.
The authority part has an empty `members` array and zero source-file totals.
Every later `source-files` part carries its own unique original paths.
The union must equal the complete original regular-file tree.

The receiver derives the exact original commit body from a captured
`commitText` or the GitHub verification payload and signature. In the signed
GitHub form, a final signature newline can create an additional continuation
line in the commit object; its bytes must be preserved. The resulting original
commit ID must match before cache creation. A GitData response without exact
raw bytes or a reconstructable signed payload needs its original raw
`commitText`; normalized date fields alone do not preserve timezone offsets.

### Exact commit bytes for an existing unsigned transfer

An existing unsigned source carrier can retain a GitData response whose dates
are normalized to UTC while its original Git commit recorded another timezone.
Receive that same carrier with the exact original commit object body in a
separate UTF-8 file:

```sh
python3 /existing/toolkit/git-object-receiving.py \
  --source-transfer /private/original-source/SOURCE_TRANSFER.json \
  --commit ORIGINAL_COMMIT \
  --commit-text /private/original-source/ORIGINAL_COMMIT.txt \
  --directory /private/original-source-receiving
```

The file contains only the complete original Git commit body: tree and ordered
parent headers, original author and committer lines, any original signature
headers, one empty line, and the exact message bytes. Preserve its final newline
state. Obtain it from the original Git object or an already captured body whose
Git commit hash equals `--commit`.

The receiver reads one canonical absolute regular file and checks its complete
Git commit identity against the transfer index before cache creation. That
identity also must match the requested commit and the existing full tree.
A different explicit body fails before receiving. The original index, carrier
archives, manifests and source objects retain their existing identities.

`--commit-text` belongs to `--source-transfer`. Metadata-based receiving already
carries its original `commitText` directly in the metadata file. Existing signed
and captured-commit transfers continue with their original command. For a new
carrier, an exact original `commitText` can be retained in its commit authority
before the authority manifest is frozen.

### Receiving, interruption and reuse

Before creating the cache, the receiver opens each original regular ZIP,
checks its recorded size, computes its full SHA-256, checks its pinned manifest
and reconstructs its carrier root tree. It also reconstructs the original
signed commit and every original directory tree. The complete partition must
preserve every original path, mode, blob ID and byte length.

During import, every regular source member is read through its ZIP checksum
and checked against its original Git blob ID. Existing exact objects are
reused. Source members are written through the same synced, immutable Git
object writer used by the other receiving modes. The original limits remain
2 MiB per source file and 128 MiB across the complete source.

`source-receiving.json` retains a `sourceTransfer` record with the exact
index file SHA-256 and each completed part's archive digest, size, carrier
identities, source totals and first receiving time. Completion is saved after
each part. Repeating the same original invocation reuses verified source
objects and continues that cache. Keep the original index and ZIP bytes while
the receiving operation is active; the source and transfer identity remain
fixed on resume.

The normal `OBJECTS_AVAILABLE` result and `repository.git` output feed
the existing builder. Source transfer changes neither the selected product
commit nor the original release, runtime installation, merchant workspace,
customer receiving or payment identities.

## Continue the original builder and runtime

Invoke the maintained builder against the receiving repository:

```js
const release = await buildDistribution({
  repository: '/private/source-receiving/repository.git',
  ref: 'ORIGINAL_COMMIT',
  output: '/private/original-release-operation',
  offline: true,
  onProgress: value => process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(value) + '\n'),
});
```

Use the maintained object receiver, builder and runtime installer with compatible
source and package limits. Keep their toolkit location separate when receiving a
historical source edition. The current `MAX_SOURCE_BYTES` shared by `build.mjs` and
`git-source.mjs` permits 128 MiB of aggregate source; this receiver uses the same
budget. `MAX_SOURCE_FILE_BYTES` retains the 2 MiB individual source limit. The
builder also checks that the complete unpacked package, including its generated
manifest and package metadata, fits the installer's 128 MiB limit. Compressed
archives remain bounded to 64 MiB, and each installed member remains bounded to
4 MiB. A toolkit retaining the earlier 64 MiB unpacked limit cannot receive a
larger cumulative package; use the current maintained installer for that package.
The selected source commit, cache identity and previous READY runtime remain
unchanged when receiving an earlier original archive.

The builder resolves its original declared commands, exports, browser assets,
and static imports. If it requests an additional original source path outside
the initial selection, add it to the same cache using repeatable
`--additional-path path/from/the/original/tree.mjs` arguments. These additions
are retained for later receiving resumes. Every added path must belong to the
same original tree and fit the same source limits.

The resulting archive and its actual digest go through the original
`upgradeRuntime` or workspace upgrade action. The previous READY runtime
remains available for its existing customers. The new runtime retains its own
source, profile, installation, managed release, and Applications identities.

## Receiving continuity and sharing

The cache has an exclusive local receiving lease and retains its original
source/metadata digest in `source-receiving.json`. Repeating the same operation
reuses complete verified objects. New objects and materialized source files are
written to temporary files and linked into place only after their full bytes
are synced. Original objects remain immutable.

The tree metadata includes the full repository. The cache initially holds the
selected native source blobs; other repository blobs can be received later
against the same original tree. Its `shallow` record preserves the commit's
actual parent IDs while allowing this one selected snapshot to stand alone.

A second original consumer can read this completed cache as its own Git donor.
It can materialize its required source closure with `--materialize` in that
consumer's private directory. Existing files must match the same original
bytes and Git executable class. New source members receive their original
0644 or 0755 mode explicitly before being synced and linked, independently of
the caller's umask. A complete native source materialization does not require another
package build or dependency install.

Keep the cache and its metadata for the active receiving operations. Publish
the maintained source implementation and the original operation result through
the existing source owner, so following consumers reuse the same received
objects and package lineage.

## Completed original receiving operation

The original MPP source selection `9ef475062876557d6baf14e0e5414d7afbf3bc7f` was received and materialized on 2026-10-12. Git enumerated all 5,077 original file entries from the reconstructed commit and its 867 verified directory-tree objects. The selected native closure contained 2,698 regular files totaling 34,580,093 bytes, including the original merchant MCP operating command. The existing read-only Git donor supplied 2,667 exact blobs; the captured incoming carrier supplied the remaining 26 unique blobs. Receiving and materialization reported `OBJECTS_AVAILABLE` with zero missing objects.

The canonical metadata SHA-256 is `ff716cd6384798f415182f2c752c7a5287f96e6c94bfaa97d1e9116117485a40`. Its complete compressed carrier is 272,442 bytes, SHA-256 `0eea1c3f8f73488f31ad0a944db4fb7728447956653f9a0de90e9b6ebd7ca7c0`. The original root tree is `50d4476a168fbe24f506a4a2297a940a9029dc25`. The same receiver can resume this source in another owned directory from the retained metadata and captured blobs, with the existing donor available read only. A following source edition has its own immutable metadata and cache identity and may reuse these completed objects as a donor.

# Customer runtime installation and recovery

Install one original Starforge merchant archive with the native dependencies selected from that archive's own declarations. The installer retains the original package at `DIRECTORY/package/`, places the selected dependency tree at `DIRECTORY/node_modules/`, and returns both absolute roots for the original host, container, and release workflows.

Each installation occupies a new private directory. An upgrade prepares a second directory and preserves the previous one for the existing deployment workflow's rollback.

## Requirements and command entry

Use Linux with Node.js 22.16 or newer, Python 3.11 or newer, npm, and the `flock` command from util-linux. A selected original dependency manifest can require a newer Node version; the resolved profile records the effective requirement. The parent directory must already exist at its real absolute path. The installer creates its child directory with mode `0700` for the current operator.

Run the maintained toolkit's `starforge runtime-install` command. The equivalent direct source entry is:

```sh
node /absolute/maintained/source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-install-cli.mjs --help
```

The maintained installer can consume an earlier original archive. Its runtime selection comes from that selected archive's source, even when the installer itself comes from a newer toolkit. Use the maintained command for subsequent installation and recovery operations; `run` dispatches into the selected archive's own original CLI.

## Complete source package limits

The maintained source archive can contain up to 128 MiB of unpacked file content,
including all source files, the complete source manifest, package metadata, README
and license. The compressed archive remains limited to 64 MiB; every installed
member remains limited to 4 MiB, and the original archive inventory must contain
at most 10,000 entries. The builder separately limits each source file to
2 MiB and checks the complete package before materialization.

Use this edition's maintained installer and `runtime-unpack.py` when the selected
cumulative archive exceeds an earlier toolkit's 64 MiB unpacked limit. The
current installer continues to accept earlier original archives. Archive and
member hashes, normalized paths, regular-file restrictions, exact source inventory
and original installation/profile identity are verified as before.

## Prepare, install, and run

Choose a new directory and supply the original archive together with its complete SHA-256 digest:

```sh
starforge runtime-install prepare \
  --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-01 \
  --archive /srv/starforge/downloads/original-merchant.tgz \
  --sha256 REPLACE_WITH_ORIGINAL_ARCHIVE_SHA256 \
  --operator

starforge runtime-install install --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-01

starforge runtime-install inspect \
  --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-01 --load --source

starforge runtime-install run \
  --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-01 -- source
```

Preparation verifies the archive digest, original manifest, original package metadata, and every declared source file before selecting the runtime profile. The original source paths and package bytes are retained. The preparation result includes the source commit, package version, profile identity, selected dependencies, entrypoint, `sourceRoot`, and `dependencyRoot`.

Installation uses npm's configured registry and cache. It extracts the generated exact dependency selection with lifecycle scripts disabled, writes a dependency lock, and checks that the selected package versions resolve and import from the original source locations. A selected dependency with an explicit native preparation declaration then runs its supported original install hook under the same installation lock. Readiness includes an actual operation of that native binding. A populated npm cache can be used explicitly:

```sh
starforge runtime-install install \
  --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-01 \
  --offline --cache /srv/starforge/npm-cache
```

The first installation uses `npm install`. A retained lock selects `npm ci` for a subsequent installation attempt. Both explicitly select local project mode, disable workspaces, and set the prefix to this runtime directory, so inherited global, location, workspace, or prefix configuration cannot redirect installation. They also use `--ignore-scripts`, `--no-audit`, `--no-fund`, `--legacy-peer-deps`, a hoisted dependency layout, and omission of development dependencies. The exact selected top-level versions live in the profile; the resulting lock retains the resolved transitive dependency tree.

Once the installation is `READY`, original commands can create and operate a merchant workspace outside the runtime directory:

```sh
starforge runtime-install run \
  --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-01 -- \
  init --dir /srv/starforge/workspaces/merchant --template application

starforge runtime-install run \
  --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-01 -- \
  run --workspace /srv/starforge/workspaces/merchant --operations-port 8081
```

The original workspace launcher owns merchant behavior and its configuration. Its default launch serves challenge-only requests. Pass the original facilitator and operator options when configuring native payment operation. `run` forwards arguments as an argument array and forwards shutdown signals to the original command.

## Select dependencies from the original release

Preparation without `--native` or `--feature` selects the base profile. `--native` includes the original native payment peers. Repeat `--feature NAME` for the original optional adapter groups required by the merchant. `--operator` records the Linux, Python, and `flock` host requirements in the profile.

For example, a new native PostgreSQL runtime can be prepared with:

```sh
starforge runtime-install prepare \
  --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-postgres-01 \
  --archive /srv/starforge/downloads/original-merchant.tgz \
  --sha256 REPLACE_WITH_ORIGINAL_ARCHIVE_SHA256 \
  --native --feature postgres --operator
```

Use the companion `runtime-profile catalog --source-root ABSOLUTE_ORIGINAL_SOURCE_ROOT` command to inspect the groups declared by a selected source tree. [RUNTIME.md](RUNTIME.md) describes profile resolution, source identity, package probes, and compatible explicit pins.

An original exact declaration keeps that exact version. For an original supported range, the resolver records the requested range and selects its declared compatible baseline unless an explicit compatible pin is supplied. `--pins FILE.json` accepts an object mapping package names to exact versions, for example:

```json
{
  "@stellar/stellar-sdk": "16.3.1"
}
```

The resolver checks an explicit pin against every selected declaration for that package. It rejects an incompatible version or a pin for an unselected dependency. Import and native operation failures remain visible in inspection and must be resolved in the selected runtime before it becomes `READY`.

## Native SQLite preparation and restart

The optional `node-agents` feature comes from the original [Node agent runtime manifest](../sf88-operator-buyer-cli/node/examples/agents/runtime-package.json). Its `better-sqlite3` dependency is explicitly marked `native: "sqlite"` in the maintained distribution. The runtime profile retains that declaration and exact version. Ordinary feature selection does not execute other packages' lifecycle scripts.

```sh
starforge runtime-install prepare \
  --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/node-agents-01 \
  --archive /srv/starforge/downloads/original-merchant.tgz \
  --sha256 REPLACE_WITH_ORIGINAL_ARCHIVE_SHA256 \
  --feature node-agents --operator

starforge runtime-install install --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/node-agents-01
starforge runtime-install inspect --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/node-agents-01 --load
starforge runtime-install run --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/node-agents-01 -- buyer-agent --help
```

After the initial script-free npm install, the installer records the resolved dependency lock before native preparation. It checks the selected package's identity, exact version, original install hook and local installation path, then runs `npm rebuild better-sqlite3@EXACT_VERSION` with lifecycle execution enabled for that declared package. The generated package also carries its explicit npm lifecycle allowance. All npm operations keep the original private project scope and retained flock descriptor.

The package's own hook selects a matching prebuilt binary or builds its bundled SQLite source with node-gyp. A source build needs Python, make and a C/C++ compiler; the existing installation log records their actual outcome. Native preparation leaves the dependency lock unchanged. The isolated readiness child opens SQLite, performs a transaction and read, obtains the SQLite version and closes the database. It records Node version, native module ABI, platform and architecture. This check also runs when `--load` is omitted; that option controls the other selected import probes. It uses an in-memory database and leaves customer stores outside the runtime untouched.

A failed or interrupted native preparation retains `dependencyInstall`, `stage`, `nativePreparation` and the current log in `install-state.json`. Resume the same original directory:

```sh
starforge runtime-install resume --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/node-agents-01
```

When the retained profile, lock and dependency imports still match, resume continues the native stage without running npm ci over that tree. If the binding already works, it adopts the completed attempt. A surviving npm child retains the original kernel lock until that child exits, so an interrupted parent cannot create a second writer.

### Offline source preparation

The prebuild downloader used by better-sqlite3 does not implement npm's offline mode. For an offline native build, the installer invokes the package's original `build-release` command directly and gives node-gyp verified local Node headers as explicit arguments. It validates that source command and its lifecycle hooks along with the package identity. The prebuild downloader is not invoked, so its configuration cannot override offline source preparation. A header prefix must contain `include/node/node_version.h`, `config.gypi`, `common.gypi`, `node.h` and `node_api.h`. The version and module ABI must match the Node executable running this installation.

```sh
starforge runtime-install resume \
  --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/node-agents-01 \
  --offline --cache /srv/starforge/npm-cache \
  --node-headers /srv/toolchains/node-24.19.0
```

The installer also checks the running Node prefix and the usual local node-gyp header caches when no prefix is supplied. Missing or mismatched headers leave a concrete native preparation error and the resolved dependency tree for the same resume command. An already working binding passes its native check without a rebuild. `--node-headers` can also select a matching local source build for an online install, upgrade or recovery.

A completed runtime is checked again before an original command is launched. If the Node ABI, installed binding, selected source or lock changes, use the original fresh-directory `recover` workflow. The new directory installs the same transitive lock and prepares its binding for the current host; the previous runtime remains available to the original activation and rollback workflow.

For the complete customer checkpoint, purchase recovery and tool workflow, continue with [NODE_AGENTS.md](NODE_AGENTS.md). The original engine and framework integration are in [PR1201](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/pull/1201); installed aliases and feature selection are in [PR1246](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/pull/1246).

Native preparation uses the documented [npm rebuild lifecycle and exact package selector](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-rebuild/), the package's [prebuild source-mode option](https://github.com/prebuild/prebuild-install#help) and [node-gyp local header support](https://github.com/nodejs/node-gyp#command-options).

## Observe and resume an interrupted installation

`inspect` returns the recorded phase and current readiness report. `--load` imports the selected package entrypoints; `--source` checks the complete retained original package against the original archive and manifest. Without `--source`, inspection still verifies the installation plan, profile identity, selected source declarations, package versions, and dependency-lock identity.

| Recorded phase | Meaning and operation |
| --- | --- |
| `PREPARED` | Original archive and profile are ready for `install`. |
| `INSTALLING` | An npm attempt was started; `resume` checks the live installation before choosing another attempt. |
| `FAILED` | The retained attempt needs inspection or resumption; its log and error remain available. |
| `READY` | The completed installation has a recorded lock and matched selected runtime. `install` can reopen it after inspection. |

Resume a prepared or interrupted installation in its existing directory:

```sh
starforge runtime-install resume \
  --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-01 --offline \
  --cache /srv/starforge/npm-cache
```

`resume` uses the same operation as `install`. If an interrupted attempt already left matching dependencies, successful imports, and a dependency lock, the installer records that existing completion and returns `recoveredExistingInstall: true`. It keeps the original attempt count and avoids another npm invocation.

The installer uses a retained Linux kernel file lock. The npm child inherits that lock, so a still-running npm process continues to exclude another writer if its parent disappears. A concurrent installer returns `RUNTIME_INSTALL_ALREADY_RUNNING` and CLI exit code `75`. Leave the lock file in place and resume after the active process finishes. Other CLI failures return `1`; successful commands return `0`. An inspection whose readiness result is false also returns `1`.

If a previously ready runtime's dependency tree or recorded lock changes, recover it into a new directory. This preserves the previous runtime path for the original deployment workflow.

## Upgrade and recover into a new directory

Upgrade supplies a new original archive and digest. Unspecified native, feature, operator, and explicit-pin selections are inherited from the previous runtime and resolved against the new archive's declarations:

```sh
starforge runtime-install upgrade \
  --from /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-01 \
  --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-02 \
  --archive /srv/starforge/downloads/original-merchant-new.tgz \
  --sha256 REPLACE_WITH_NEW_ORIGINAL_ARCHIVE_SHA256

starforge runtime-install compare \
  --before /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-01 \
  --after /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-02
```

The comparison reports source and profile identities plus added, removed, or changed dependency versions. An exact recovery preserves the original selection and archive:

```sh
starforge runtime-install recover \
  --from /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-01 \
  --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-recovered-01 \
  --offline --cache /srv/starforge/npm-cache
```

When the previous complete plan has the same source and profile, recovery carries its dependency lock into the new directory and installs with `npm ci`. A ready source runtime must still match its recorded lock before that lock is carried forward.

The same `recover` command also handles interruption during archive copying, extraction, or later preparation. It reads the retained `preparation.json` options, checks the retained archive's digest, and prepares the original source again in the new directory. If copying the archive was itself interrupted, recovery uses the explicitly retained original input path with the same expected digest. Keep that original input available until preparation has finished. The recovery result includes `recoveredPreparation: true` when this path was used. The selected Python executable is retained and reused.

### Hand the runtime to the existing deployment workflow

Use the returned absolute `sourceRoot` and `dependencyRoot` together when preparing the original host, container, or SF46 release workflow. A runtime at `/srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-02` has:

| Deployment input | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `sourceRoot` | `/srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-02/package/source` |
| `dependencyRoot` | `/srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-02` |
| Original CLI entrypoint | `/srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-02/package/source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/cli.mjs` |

# Transfer a ready runtime to an offline host

Move an existing Starforge runtime's original release and exact dependency selection to another operator host. The receiver reconstructs the selected source and public npm package archives, populates its own cache, and installs through the maintained [runtime installer](RUNTIME_INSTALL.md). The original source, profile and dependency lock remain the inputs throughout.

The same workflow is available through `starforge runtime-transfer` and the Runtime Workspace. Use the current maintained toolkit to receive an older original release. The installed merchant's own commands continue to come from that selected release.

## What the transfer contains

| Retained input | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `source.tgz` | Exact archive from the selected original runtime. |
| `runtime-profile.json` | Original feature selection, exact dependency declarations and host requirements. |
| `package.json` | Original generated dependency package for that profile. |
| `package-lock.json` | Exact accepted transitive dependency lock from the ready installation. |
| `artifacts/<sha256>.tgz` | Original public npm tarballs selected by the lock, deduplicated by their retained bytes. |

The exported `manifest.json` identifies those files, their byte lengths and SHA-256 values, the npm integrity values, the original runtime identities, the complete payload digest and an ordered list of parts. Its schema is `stellar-forge.runtime-transfer.v1`. Each part has an index, filename, offset, byte length and SHA-256.

Send the exact manifest bytes and the declared files from `parts/`. A part is at most 8 MiB; the default maximum complete payload is 2 GiB. The parts are segments of the file payload, so keep the manifest's filenames and indexes. They are not individual compressed archives.

The transfer covers the selected release and its public package dependencies. Merchant configuration, wallets, database contents, provider credentials, saved business requests, private registry packages and operating-system tools continue through their existing installation and backup workflows. An npm source transfer carries the original package archives; a native image is handled by [the image workflow](runtime-workspace/IMAGE_OPERATIONS.md).

## Use the receiving host's existing tools

Use the original installer's Linux host requirements: Node.js 22.16 or later, Python 3.11 or later, npm and util-linux `flock`. A selected profile can require a newer Node version. The selected runtime's `host` and dependency declarations identify that requirement.

Choose real absolute paths whose parents already exist. Keep three distinct locations: the sending runtime, the exported transfer, and the receiving transfer. Prepare the new runtime outside the receiving transfer directory. The commands create private final directories for the current operator; use their returned paths on later calls.

For source-checkout operation, the command entry is:

~~~sh
node /absolute/maintained/source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-transfer-cli.mjs --help
~~~

The following examples use `starforge runtime-transfer`, the installed alias for that same command. Substitute the actual retained paths and digests supplied by your own operation.

## 1. Review the original installation

~~~sh
starforge runtime-transfer review \
  --runtime /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-01
~~~

Review reopens the original runtime inspector, checks its complete source and recorded lock, and returns the selected source, profile, package and dependency inventory. The sender must be an unchanged original `READY` installation. If its original inspector reports a changed lock, source or native binding, complete its existing installation recovery before exporting it.

The response includes:

- `runtime`: original installation ID, source commit, package name/version and archive/profile/package/lock hashes.
- `selection`, `host` and `dependencies`: the original profile and its requirements.
- `inventory`: every retained lock location, distinct public artifacts, bundled locations and concrete unsupported entries.
- `ready`: whether this reviewed inventory can use the transfer format.

Use `runtime.lockSha256` as the exact `--expect-lock` value during export. This binds the export to the installation you reviewed.

The supported npm locks are version 2 or 3 with an explicit `packages` inventory. Public tarballs must resolve to credential-free HTTPS URLs on `registry.npmjs.org` and have a supported integrity value. Bundled and optional locations remain identified. A local link, Git dependency, private or other registry location is returned as a specific unsupported entry; its original source is not silently substituted. Keep the selected lock unchanged and use that dependency's original distribution route.

## 2. Export from the populated source cache

~~~sh
starforge runtime-transfer export \
  --runtime /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-01 \
  --directory /srv/starforge/transfers/merchant-01 \
  --cache /srv/starforge/npm-cache \
  --expect-lock EXACT_REVIEWED_LOCK_SHA256
~~~

Export uses the explicitly selected cache in offline mode by default. For each distinct locked public package it asks npm for that exact tarball, verifies the lock's integrity value, retains the original bytes, then streams the complete file payload into the declared parts. It does not repackage the installed dependency folders.

If an approved connected sending host needs to fetch a missing public tarball, select `--online` when creating its export. This enables the exact public-registry acquisition; it does not change the accepted lock or dependency versions. An existing export binds its offline/online mode, cache path and part size. To change one of those selections, create a new transfer directory while retaining the prior incomplete export. `--npm` selects an existing npm executable. `--part-bytes` accepts 65,536 through 8,388,608 bytes.

An interrupted export retains its source/profile/lock binding, completed package receipts and progress. Repeat the same export with the same final transfer directory and original inputs to continue it. A changed bound input is an explicit conflict.

Finish with a full part read:

~~~sh
starforge runtime-transfer inspect \
  --directory /srv/starforge/transfers/merchant-01 --verify
~~~

Retain the returned `manifestSha256` and `manifest.transferId`. The sending state reaches `COMPLETE` when this source carrier is complete. That state describes the exported data, not a receiving installation.

Provide the receiver with `manifest.json`, its exact SHA-256 and the declared `parts/part-00000.bin` style files. Keep the manifest bytes unchanged: reformatting its JSON changes the expected manifest digest. The receiver can obtain parts in several transfers and resume after an interrupted download.

## 3. Receive and reopen the same transfer

With all currently available part files in one directory:

~~~sh
starforge runtime-transfer receive \
  --directory /srv/starforge/receiving/merchant-01 \
  --manifest /srv/starforge/downloads/manifest.json \
  --sha256 EXACT_MANIFEST_SHA256 \
  --parts /srv/starforge/downloads/parts
~~~

The receiver verifies the supplied manifest digest before accepting its identity. It imports the available missing parts by the exact declared names. Missing files stay visible in the result; an intact cohort is reconstructed and its private cache is populated automatically.

Reopen that same receive directory with the same manifest and digest after a lost response. The original transfer ID stays bound to the directory.

To deliver a particular part separately:

~~~sh
starforge runtime-transfer receive-part \
  --directory /srv/starforge/receiving/merchant-01 \
  --index 0 \
  --file /srv/starforge/downloads/parts/part-00000.bin

starforge runtime-transfer inspect \
  --directory /srv/starforge/receiving/merchant-01 --verify
~~~

Use the actual part's index, filename and digest from the manifest. Inspection returns each part's status and explicit `missingParts` and `invalidParts` indexes. With `--verify`, present files are hashed rather than accepted only by their length. Exact repeats reopen the same retained part.

After all parts are available:

~~~sh
starforge runtime-transfer complete \
  --directory /srv/starforge/receiving/merchant-01
~~~

Completion checks the whole payload, reconstructs only the declared file set, verifies each original file and npm package integrity, and populates `RECEIVER/cache` through explicit npm cache additions. It retains per-artifact cache progress for the same continuation.

Use `complete --files-only` when the immediate handoff should reconstruct the original files without populating the cache. The result is `RECEIVED`; a later ordinary `complete` continues to `CACHE_READY`. Keep the immutable source cohort available even after cache population: npm's cache is a working cache, while these original files and manifest are the retained transfer.

## 4. Install at its final runtime path

~~~sh
starforge runtime-transfer install \
  --directory /srv/starforge/receiving/merchant-01 \
  --runtime /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-received-01
~~~

The transfer completes and checks its received files and cache, then calls the original preparer and installer with `offline: true`. It supplies the original archive, selection and exact lock in a new final runtime directory. The retained lock makes the original installer use its existing `npm ci` path with the maintained installation flags.

The result contains `status`, `transferId`, `manifestSha256`, `runtimeDirectory`, the retained transfer installation `record`, and the original installer `result`. Successful installation is followed by the original full source/import/native readiness inspection and exact lock comparison.

Add `--prepare-only` to stop after the original `PREPARED` state. Later, repeat the same transfer `install` with the same target and the same Python/header binding to perform installation. `--python` and `--npm` select the already available executables.

### Native dependencies use the receiving host

For a selected native SQLite dependency, the maintained installer prepares and operates the original binding for the receiving Node version, module ABI, operating system and architecture. The sending host's ready binary is not part of this tarball transfer.

Offline SQLite source preparation needs the original host compiler tools: Python, make, a C/C++ compiler and matching local Node headers. Supply a matching existing header prefix when needed:

~~~sh
starforge runtime-transfer install \
  --directory /srv/starforge/receiving/merchant-01 \
  --runtime /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-received-01 \
  --node-headers /srv/toolchains/current-node
~~~

The prefix contains the original `include/node` files, including `node_version.h`, `config.gypi`, `common.gypi`, `node.h` and `node_api.h`. The installer checks their Node version and ABI. Its offline path invokes the supported package's original source-build command without invoking the network prebuild downloader. The original installation log and native preparation state explain missing or mismatched host inputs.

Choose those host inputs before the first transfer installation request; they form part of the retained request binding. A successful dependency receive does not declare a native binding ready. See [Native SQLite preparation and restart](RUNTIME_INSTALL.md#native-sqlite-preparation-and-restart) for the original behavior and readiness operation.

## 5. Recover and hand off the installation

For an interrupted npm/native stage, inspect the original runtime and continue the same target through the same transfer install command. The original installer's kernel lease, attempt log and retained lock decide whether to adopt completed work or continue preparation. Keep an active installation's lock and original operation intact.

If preparation did not commit a usable runtime plan, recover its retained intent into a new final directory:

~~~sh
starforge runtime-transfer recover \
  --directory /srv/starforge/receiving/merchant-01 \
  --from /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-received-01 \
  --runtime /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-recovered-01
~~~

Supply the same required `--python` and `--node-headers` selections for the receiving host. Recovery checks that its previous runtime belongs to this original transfer, then delegates to the maintained new-directory recovery operation. It does not replace the previous directory or create a second merchant request.

Once the returned status is `READY`, use the original command to inspect and run that installation:

~~~sh
starforge runtime-install inspect \
  --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-recovered-01 --load --source

starforge runtime-install run \
  --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/merchant-recovered-01 -- source
~~~

Open the actual runtime in [Runtime Workspace](runtime-workspace/README.md). Its existing deployment handoff supplies both `sourceRoot` and `dependencyRoot`. The original managed release workflow owns adoption, activation and rollback. Keep those absolute runtime paths when handing them to the host or image operator.

## Read the state at the correct stage

| State or result | Completed work | Continue with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Export `PACKAGES` / `PARTS` | Original dependency acquisition or part writing is in progress. | Repeat the same export inputs and directory. |
| Export `COMPLETE` | Manifest and complete source carrier exist. | Send exact manifest and declared parts. |
| Receive `RECEIVING` | Manifest retained; some parts may be missing. | Inspect and deliver the identified parts. |
| Receive `RECEIVED` | Original files reconstructed and verified. | Complete cache population. |
| Receive `CACHE_READY` | Received package cohort has populated this receiver's cache. | Install into a new runtime directory. |
| Runtime `PREPARED` | Original archive, profile and lock are prepared. | Original offline installation. |
| Runtime `READY` | Original installed source, dependency lock, imports and selected native binding passed readiness. | Original merchant/deployment operation. |

The receive result's `complete` field describes its declared parts. The original installation result is the authority for runtime readiness.

A manifest mismatch means the supplied bytes do not match the selected manifest SHA. A part hash or length mismatch identifies the exact part to obtain again from its original source. Keep the manifest, its state and any conflict result; if immutable existing bytes conflict, use a new receive directory with that same manifest instead of changing its recorded identities.

| `installReceivedRuntime({ directory, runtimeDirectory, recoverFrom, ... })` | Original offline preparation, installation or new-directory recovery. |

Use exact UTF-8 manifest bytes or the original manifest string for receiving, and the supplied SHA-256. Export, completion and installation accept an abort signal and progress callback; part receiving accepts an abort signal. Keep the current returned `directory`, `manifestSha256`, `manifest.transferId`, `cacheDirectory` and `filesDirectory`; later requests should reopen that same state.

The source carrier's immutable file set and the receiver's operating state have different lifetimes. Retain the manifest and source parts for receiving or rebuilding the explicit cache, plus the original runtime's installation records for operational recovery. Source transfer does not activate a managed release automatically.

## Maintain a recipe

Recipes live in `distribution/selections/ID.json` and use schema
`stellar-forge.distribution-source-selection.v1`. The filename must match the ID.
`base.commands` and `base.exports` explicitly name existing base declarations;
`base.features` names the original feature or package-manifest groups.
`base.applicationProviders` and `base.merchantProviders` name base providers
when the base declares any. `base.browserAssets` selects an existing base browser
server and its original mapping manifest.

`contributions` selects complete existing contribution IDs. The builder composes
them after base selection; a conflict between included owners remains an error.
Unselected contributions do not participate. Their source ownership, command
descriptions, providers, dependencies, browser assets and support files remain
the original contribution's declarations.

`components` selects complete original directory roots; `supportFiles` selects
explicit original files. Optional `excludeFiles` adds exact file exclusions to
the original base exclusions. A required command, export, provider, runtime
manifest or static import cannot be excluded successfully. The optional
`product` object selects existing source README/bin and product metadata through
the maintained product-package contract. When that object omits `repository`,
the selected product inherits only `base.product.repository` when present.
An explicit recipe repository remains authoritative. README and executable
selection continue to use the recipe and the original product-package defaults;
unrelated base executables are not inherited. If the base has no repository
override, the maintained package default remains in effect. This keeps a
standalone product's source identity without bringing other products' bins
into its selected archive.

Required command and export targets, selected provider modules, runtime package
manifests, and browser server/manifests are retained as explicit runtime seeds.
The original static ESM and browser-map closure then includes their dependencies.
Complete component directories retain Python modules, template files, generated
plugin inputs, browser resources and other paths loaded dynamically. A new
product recipe therefore needs its original operational receiving journey,
including restart and downloaded files, as well as a successful build. Static
module closure cannot prove that a dynamically constructed pathname is present.

Installed declaration reading checks the original recipe and every contribution
against the retained file inventory. A runtime cannot switch recipes or add an
unselected registration file inside an existing selected package.
